intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Pass through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and traditional Gurung villages while enjoying breathtaking views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. This is the crown jewel of Himalayan trekking experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in a panoramic 180-degree view. The short but rewarding hike takes about 1.5 hours from Ghorepani village.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Homestay
experiences.description: Stay overnight in a traditional Gurung ethnic village and immerse yourself in local mountain culture. Share home-cooked dal bhat meals with a local family, learn about ancient shamanic traditions, observe traditional weaving, and hear folk stories around a fire. A deeply authentic and humbling cultural exchange.

experiences.name: Modi Khola River Valley Nature Walk
experiences.description: Explore the lush subtropical lower valleys of the Modi Khola river corridor, rich with diverse flora and fauna. Spot Himalayan wildlife including langur monkeys, colorful pheasants, and rare birds amid dense rhododendron and bamboo forests. A guided nature walk reveals medicinal plants and ecological wonders unique to this biodiversity hotspot.
experiences.location: Modi Khola River Valley, Lower Annapurna Foothills

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek and High Camp Overnight
experiences.description: Trek the less-crowded Mardi Himal trail to High Camp at 3,580m for stunning close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) and the Annapurna massif. This off-the-beaten-path route offers solitude, pristine alpine meadows, and dramatic ridge walking with far fewer trekkers than the main circuits, making it a hidden gem for nature lovers.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal, Eastern Annapurna Conservation Area

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked budget taxi or airport bus to your accommodation. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in Annapurna region. Freshen up and get a good night's rest to prepare for the trek ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or dal bhat from a local teahouse near the resort if still open upon arrival, approximately NPR 200–350

day_by_day.notes: Late arrival day — prioritize rest. Exchange some USD to NPR at the airport for immediate expenses. Keep NPR 500–1000 handy for transport and tips. Confirm trekking permits needed (ACAP and TIMS card) for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to the nearest permit office (Pokhara or local ACAP counter) to obtain your Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) and TIMS card. ACAP costs NPR 3000 for foreigners, TIMS NPR 2000. Explore the local Pokhara lakeside area (Phewa Lake) on foot — enjoy the mountain views and local market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) via a short hike or budget boat ride across Phewa Lake (NPR 200 round trip). The pagoda offers stunning panoramic views of the Annapurna range. Walk back down and stroll through the Lakeside Bazaar for budget trekking gear if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Lakeside Thamel area of Pokhara. Browse local shops for any last-minute trekking supplies. Attend a free cultural show at a local restaurant if available. Plan and review your trekking route for the coming days.

meals.breakfast: Dal bhat or egg and toast at a local teahouse near the resort, NPR 150–250
meals.lunch: Thukpa (Tibetan noodle soup) or momos at a lakeside budget restaurant, NPR 200–300
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal at a local Nepali restaurant in Pokhara Lakeside, NPR 300–450

day_by_day.notes: Secure all permits today before heading into the mountains. Carry your passport for permit registration. Start hydrating well and avoid alcohol to acclimatize. Budget for the day: approximately NPR 6000–7000 including permits.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early local bus or shared jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (approximately 1.5–2 hours, NPR 200–300). Begin the classic Annapurna Circuit / Poon Hill trek. Start trekking from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 3–4 hours, 7 km). Walk through terraced fields, suspension bridges, and rhododendron forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga toward Ulleri (approximately 1.5 hours, steep stone staircase of ~3000 steps). Take breaks to enjoy views of the Modi Khola river valley. Arrive at Ulleri and check into a budget teahouse lodge (NPR 200–400 per night, often free with meal purchase).
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse, interact with fellow trekkers, and enjoy the crisp mountain air. Watch the sunset over the Annapurna foothills from Ulleri village. Rest early to prepare for the next day's trek.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or chapati with tea at the resort before departure, NPR 150–200
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or dal bhat at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga, NPR 250–350
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with vegetables at Ulleri teahouse, NPR 300–400

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper trekking boots for the Ulleri stone staircase — it is very steep. Carry at least 2 liters of water. October is peak trekking season with clear skies and excellent Himalayan views. Budget for the day: NPR 1500–2500 excluding permits.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning start from Ulleri. Trek through dense rhododendron and oak forests toward Ghorepani (approximately 3–4 hours, 8 km, gradual climb). Enjoy views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South as you ascend. Arrive at Ghorepani village (2860m) and check into a budget teahouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and acclimatize at Ghorepani. Explore the small village, visit local tea stalls, and interact with Magar and Gurung community members. Take a short acclimatization walk around the village perimeter to help your body adjust to the altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare and set your alarm for a 4:00 AM wake-up for the Poon Hill sunrise hike the next morning. Enjoy a warm dinner and hot ginger tea or lemon honey tea at the teahouse. Stargaze from the teahouse porch — the Himalayan night sky is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or oatmeal with honey at Ulleri teahouse, NPR 200–300
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice or noodle soup at a teahouse en route, NPR 250–350
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or vegetable curry at Ghorepani teahouse, NPR 350–450

day_by_day.notes: Altitude at Ghorepani is 2860m — drink plenty of fluids and avoid overexertion. Ghorepani has multiple budget teahouses; negotiate room rates or opt for free room with meal purchase. October weather should be clear and cold at night — pack a warm sleeping bag liner.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:00 AM and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint (3210m, approximately 45 minutes). Watch the legendary sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges — one of Nepal's most iconic views. Photograph Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Annapurna I, Annapurna South, and Dhaulagiri in golden morning light. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (approximately 4–5 hours, 10 km) through beautiful rhododendron forests. The trail offers continuous Himalayan panoramas. Arrive at Tadapani teahouse and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the peaceful mountain village atmosphere of Tadapani. Write journal entries or sketch the mountain views. Have an early dinner and rest well for the continued trek tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and boiled eggs or toast at Ghorepani teahouse after Poon Hill hike, NPR 150–250
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and bread or dal bhat at a teahouse en route to Tadapani, NPR 300–400
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with lentil soup at Tadapani teahouse, NPR 350–450

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee is NPR 100. Bring a headlamp for the pre-dawn hike. It can be very cold at the summit before sunrise — wear all your layers. The Ghorepani to Tadapani trail passes through one of Nepal's finest rhododendron forests, spectacular in spring but still beautiful in October.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chomrong (approximately 4–5 hours, 10 km). The trail descends steeply through forests and crosses the Modi Khola river before climbing up to Chomrong village. Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Chomrong is the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chomrong village — a beautiful Gurung settlement with terraced fields. Visit the local ACAP checkpoint and get your permits stamped. Take a short walk to the viewpoint above the village for panoramic Himalayan views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a budget teahouse in Chomrong. Chat with fellow trekkers about trail conditions ahead. Enjoy a hot shower if available (usually NPR 200–300 extra). Plan the Annapurna Base Camp approach for the coming days.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and tea at Tadapani teahouse, NPR 200–300
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or chapati with vegetables at a teahouse en route, NPR 250–350
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with achar (pickle) at Chomrong teahouse, NPR 350–500

day_by_day.notes: Chomrong has relatively good facilities for a mountain village — ATM not available beyond this point, so carry sufficient NPR cash. Prices increase as you go higher into the sanctuary. Stock up on snacks like Snickers, biscuits, and nuts here at lower prices.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong to Dovan (approximately 5–6 hours via Sinuwa and Bamboo). The trail descends to the Modi Khola gorge and then climbs through bamboo and rhododendron forest. Pass through the ACAP checkpost at Sinuwa. The landscape becomes increasingly dramatic and enclosed by towering peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Himalayan forest to Dovan teahouse (2600m). The trail passes through dense bamboo groves — keep an eye out for Himalayan wildlife including langur monkeys and colorful pheasants. Arrive at Dovan and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the small but cozy Dovan teahouse. The gorge setting is dramatic and atmospheric. Enjoy a warm dinner and prepare for higher altitude trekking ahead. Check for any signs of altitude sickness and hydrate well.

meals.breakfast: Egg and toast or muesli at Chomrong teahouse, NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or fried noodles at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse, NPR 350–450
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice at Dovan teahouse, NPR 400–550

day_by_day.notes: Prices increase significantly inside the Annapurna Sanctuary. Expect to pay NPR 350–600 for meals at higher elevations. The trail can be slippery in shaded sections — use trekking poles. No mobile signal in most of this section.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3700m (approximately 5–6 hours via Himalaya Hotel and Deurali). The trail emerges from the forest into an open glacial valley — a dramatic moment as the sanctuary walls close in around you. The massive peaks of Annapurna III, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre dominate the skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp. Rest and acclimatize — do not rush to Annapurna Base Camp today. Take a short walk around MBC to help acclimatization. The views of the sacred Fishtail peak (Machhapuchhre) up close are absolutely stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset turn the surrounding peaks golden and pink — one of the most spectacular light shows in the Himalayas. The amphitheater of peaks surrounding MBC is awe-inspiring. Rest early for the pre-dawn push to Annapurna Base Camp tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and hot tea at Dovan, NPR 250–350
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and bread at Himalaya Hotel or Deurali teahouse, NPR 400–500
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse, NPR 500–650

day_by_day.notes: Altitude at MBC is 3700m — headaches and mild altitude sickness are common. Drink 3–4 liters of water daily. Avoid alcohol completely. Garlic soup is believed locally to help with altitude acclimatization. If you feel seriously unwell, descend immediately — do not push through severe AMS symptoms.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:30 AM for the sunrise hike to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4130m (approximately 1.5 hours from MBC). Reach ABC as the sun rises over the Annapurna range — a bucket-list Himalayan experience. You are surrounded by a 360-degree amphitheater of 7000m and 8000m peaks including Annapurna I (8091m), the 10th highest mountain in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning at ABC exploring the base camp area, visiting the memorial chortens for mountaineers, and soaking in the extraordinary mountain environment. Begin descent back to MBC and continue down to Deurali or Himalaya Hotel for lunch. Continue descending toward Bamboo teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Reach Bamboo teahouse (approximately 2310m) — the significant descent helps with altitude recovery. Celebrate reaching ABC with a well-earned hot meal. Reflect on the achievement of reaching one of Nepal's most iconic trekking destinations.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits before sunrise hike; proper breakfast at ABC or MBC after sunrise, NPR 300–450
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or dal bhat at Himalaya Hotel teahouse during descent, NPR 450–550
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with extra helpings at Bamboo teahouse — you have earned it!, NPR 400–500

day_by_day.notes: ABC summit day is the highlight of the entire trip. Start early to catch sunrise and avoid afternoon cloud buildup. Take many photos but also take time to simply stand and absorb the experience. The descent from 4130m to 2310m is long — pace yourself and protect your knees on the downhill sections.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo back to Chomrong (approximately 4–5 hours). The return journey through the rhododendron and bamboo forest feels different with fresh eyes and a sense of accomplishment. Stop at Sinuwa for tea and enjoy the views you may have rushed past on the way up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Chomrong. Take a well-deserved rest. Visit the local bakery in Chomrong — famous for apple pie and cinnamon rolls baked fresh daily. Treat yourself to a slice as a budget splurge (NPR 150–250).
day_by_day.evening: Soak tired muscles in a hot shower at the teahouse. Chat with new trekkers just beginning their Sanctuary journey. Enjoy the warm community atmosphere of Chomrong village. Sleep in a comfortable teahouse bed.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or muesli at Bamboo teahouse, NPR 250–350
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and chapati at Sinuwa teahouse, NPR 350–450
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with chicken curry (if available) at Chomrong teahouse, NPR 400–550

day_by_day.notes: Your body will feel the cumulative effect of 8 days of trekking — this is normal. Stretch your legs and back in the evening. Check your feet for blisters and treat them promptly. Tomorrow begins the final descent toward Pokhara.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong back to Ghorepani via Tadapani (approximately 5–6 hours). This is a beautiful ridge walk with continuous mountain views. The return route through the rhododendron forest to Tadapani and then on to Ghorepani is one of the most scenic sections of the entire trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani. Rest and explore the village more leisurely than on the way up. Visit the local monastery if open. Browse small handicraft stalls selling Tibetan jewelry and thangka paintings — great budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your final night in the high mountains at Ghorepani. Have a celebratory hot chocolate or masala tea. Watch the Annapurna peaks glow in the alpenglow sunset one last time. Prepare for the descent to Nayapul tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Egg bhurji (scrambled eggs) and tea at Chomrong teahouse, NPR 200–300
meals.lunch: Fried rice or thukpa at Tadapani teahouse, NPR 300–400
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with extra dal at Ghorepani teahouse, NPR 350–450

day_by_day.notes: This is one of the longer trekking days — start by 7:30 AM. The trail between Tadapani and Ghorepani has some steep sections. Pace yourself and enjoy the journey. October light in the rhododendron forest is beautiful even without flowers.

day_by_day.morning: Final mountain morning — optional short sunrise walk near Ghorepani for last Himalayan views. Trek from Ghorepani down to Ulleri and continue to Nayapul (approximately 4–5 hours, mostly downhill). The descent through terraced farmland and village paths is a pleasant end to the trekking portion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Nayapul and catch a local bus or shared jeep back to Pokhara (NPR 200–300, approximately 1.5 hours). Check back into accommodation in Pokhara. Take a long hot shower, do laundry, and rest. Walk to Phewa Lake for a peaceful lakeside sit-down.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Annapurna trek with a lakeside dinner in Pokhara. The Lakeside area has many budget restaurants with international and Nepali food. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal within budget — you deserve it!

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Ghorepani teahouse, NPR 200–300
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a local teahouse in Ulleri or Tikhedhunga, NPR 250–350
meals.dinner: Grilled fish from Phewa Lake or buff (buffalo) momos at a Pokhara Lakeside restaurant, NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Return to Pokhara marks the end of the trekking section. Visit a pharmacy if you have any blisters, muscle pain, or minor ailments. Restock your wallet — there are ATMs throughout Pokhara Lakeside. Rest well for a final day of exploration tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (NPR 300–500 per day) and explore Pokhara at your own pace. Cycle around Phewa Lake and visit the Barahi Temple on the lake island (short boat ride, NPR 100 round trip). Continue cycling to the Seti River Gorge viewpoint — a dramatic natural canyon cutting through the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry NPR 400 for foreigners) — an excellent museum dedicated to Himalayan mountaineering history, featuring exhibits on all 14 eight-thousanders and the legendary climbers who conquered them. Return bicycles and visit the Old Bazaar area of Pokhara for authentic local shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride on Phewa Lake (NPR 400–600 for a private rowboat, or join a group). Watch the Annapurna range reflected in the lake at golden hour — one of Pokhara's most iconic experiences. Browse the Lakeside night market for budget souvenirs: pashmina scarves (NPR 300–800), Thangka prints (NPR 200–500), and handmade jewelry.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with jam and butter and masala tea at a Lakeside café, NPR 150–250
meals.lunch: Newari set meal or thali at a local Nepali restaurant away from the tourist strip for authentic food at lower prices, NPR 200–350
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant — try a set meal with soup, main course, and dessert, NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara is a great place to buy trekking souvenirs and gifts. Bargaining is expected in the bazaar — start at 50% of the asking price and settle around 60–70%. The International Mountain Museum is genuinely excellent and well worth the entry fee for trekking enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Annapurna region. Wake up early for one last sunrise view of the Annapurna range from the Pokhara lakeside — free and unforgettable. Pack your bags and do a final check of your accommodation. If time permits, visit the Davis Falls (Patale Chhango) nearby — a unique waterfall that disappears into an underground gorge (entry NPR 30).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Pokhara to Kathmandu — options include tourist bus (NPR 600–800, 6–7 hours) or domestic flight (NPR 5000–8000, 25 minutes) depending on your departure schedule and budget. If flying out of Kathmandu, arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport with 3 hours to spare for international departures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations — check in for your flight, clear customs and immigration. Reflect on an incredible 14-day Annapurna adventure including Poon Hill sunrise, Annapurna Base Camp, mountain teahouse hospitality, and the natural beauty of the Himalayas. Safe travels home!

meals.breakfast: Final dal bhat or egg breakfast at a Pokhara teahouse, NPR 150–250
meals.lunch: Quick meal at Pokhara bus park or airport, or packed snacks for the journey, NPR 200–400
meals.dinner: Airport meal in Kathmandu or inflight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for Pokhara to Kathmandu travel — bus journeys can be delayed by traffic or road conditions. If taking the tourist bus, book the day before from Lakeside (NPR 600–800). Domestic flights are faster but book in advance during October peak season. Keep NPR 1695 airport departure tax handy (usually included in international ticket but verify). Final budget summary: total trip cost for 14 days estimated at NPR 35,000–55,000 (approximately USD 260–410) excluding international flights and permits paid on Day 2.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer. Check in to your Kathmandu transit hotel or head directly toward Pokhara if a night bus/transfer is pre-booked. Rest and recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light snack or dal bhat at the airport arrival lounge or a 24-hour dhaba near the airport (NPR 300–500)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely an arrival day. No sightseeing is recommended. Confirm your onward transport to Pokhara (the gateway to Annapurna) for the following morning. Keep energy drinks and snacks handy after the long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning tourist bus or private vehicle transfer from Kathmandu to Pokhara (approximately 6–7 hours, scenic Prithvi Highway route). Depart by 07:00 to maximize daylight. Enjoy views of terraced hills and the Trishuli River en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara around 13:00–14:00. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Lakeside (Phewa Lake) area. Freshen up, then take a leisurely stroll along Phewa Lake promenade. Visit the colorful local market stalls and pick up any last-minute trekking supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride on Phewa Lake to view the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) mountain reflections on the water. Explore the Lakeside bazaar and get oriented with the area.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Kathmandu hotel or packed meal for the bus (NPR 200–400)
meals.lunch: Roadside dhaba en route to Pokhara — try thukpa (noodle soup) or dal bhat (NPR 250–450)
meals.dinner: Moondance Restaurant or Caffe Concerto, Lakeside Pokhara — pasta, pizza, or Nepali set menu (NPR 600–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Alternatively, take a 25-minute domestic flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara (Buddha Air or Yeti Airlines, ~USD 100–120) to save time. Confirm trekking permits and TIMS card at the Pokhara Tourism Office tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) office and Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara to obtain your TIMS card (Trekkers' Information Management System) and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP). Cost: approximately USD 30–35 total. Pack your trekking gear and finalize day pack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a local taxi to Sarangkot Hill (30 minutes from Lakeside). Hike the moderate trail to the top of Sarangkot (1,592m) for sweeping panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. This serves as a warm-up hike (1.5–2 hours up, 1 hour down).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Pokhara Lakeside. Visit the International Mountain Museum (open until 17:00) to learn about Himalayan history and mountaineering expeditions. Relax at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort or a nearby café — eggs, toast, and tea (NPR 400–700)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or tea house snacks at Sarangkot summit — instant noodles, boiled eggs, tea (NPR 200–400)
meals.dinner: Busy Bee Café or The Laughing Buddha, Lakeside — Nepali thali or continental options (NPR 700–1,400)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season in Nepal — expect clear skies and excellent mountain views. Sarangkot is ideal for acclimatization before the main trek begins. Carry a light rain jacket just in case.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 04:30 for the iconic sunrise from Sarangkot (optional but highly recommended). Return to resort by 08:00 for breakfast. Then drive by taxi or bus to Nayapul (1.5–2 hours from Pokhara). Begin the Annapurna Circuit / Poon Hill trek. Hike from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (1,540m) — approximately 3–4 hours of moderate walking through terraced farmland and traditional Gurung villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga toward Ulleri (1,960m). The famous 3,000+ stone staircase ascent to Ulleri is challenging but rewarding. Arrive by early afternoon. Rest and explore the village.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a comfortable mid-range tea house in Ulleri. Enjoy the quiet mountain atmosphere, interact with local Gurung families, and watch the evening alpenglow on the Annapurna South face.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at resort before departure — porridge, eggs, juice (NPR 500–800)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a tea house in Tikhedhunga (NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Tea house dinner in Ulleri — dal bhat set meal with local vegetables and pickles (NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 12–14 km. Elevation gain: ~900m. Difficulty: moderate to strenuous due to the Ulleri staircase. Carry 2–3 liters of water. Trekking poles highly recommended. Start early to avoid afternoon haze.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ulleri by 07:30. Trek through rhododendron and oak forests to Ghorepani (2,860m) — approximately 4–5 hours of steady uphill walking. The trail passes through Banthanti and offers stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghorepani by early afternoon. Check in to a mid-range lodge (Hot Spring Lodge or Annapurna Guest House recommended). Rest and acclimatize. Explore the small village, visit the local monastery, and browse handicraft stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Optional short hike to the ridge above Ghorepani for sunset views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna. Return to lodge for a warm dinner and early bedtime in preparation for the Poon Hill sunrise.

meals.breakfast: Tea house breakfast in Ulleri — pancakes, honey, butter tea (NPR 350–550)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or quick stop at Banthanti tea house — soup, chocolate bar, hot lemon (NPR 300–500)
meals.dinner: Ghorepani lodge dinner — garlic soup, dal bhat, apple pie (NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 10–12 km. Elevation gain: ~900m. Ghorepani sits above 2,800m — drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol to prevent altitude sickness. Set alarm for 04:00 for tomorrow's Poon Hill sunrise hike.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 04:00. Hike by headlamp to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m) — 45 minutes to 1 hour from Ghorepani. Witness one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas, with panoramic views of Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and over 20 Himalayan peaks. Return to Ghorepani by 08:00 for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,630m) via the scenic Deurali pass and dense rhododendron forests — approximately 4–5 hours. The trail offers continuous mountain views and passes through pristine forest habitat rich in Himalayan birds.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tadapani. Check in to a cozy lodge. Relax on the terrace with mountain views. Journal, read, or simply soak in the tranquility of the high Himalayan forest.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea/coffee at Poon Hill top (vendors present), then full breakfast back at Ghorepani lodge — eggs, porridge, toast (NPR 400–700)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or Deurali tea house stop — dal bhat or noodles (NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Tadapani lodge dinner — vegetable curry, rice, lentil soup, masala tea (NPR 550–850)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of the entire Ghorepani–Poon Hill circuit. October skies are typically crystal clear — ideal photography conditions. Bring a warm layer as temperatures at Poon Hill pre-dawn can drop to 2–5°C. Trek distance today (including Poon Hill): ~16 km total.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m) — approximately 4–5 hours. The trail descends steeply through bamboo and rhododendron forest before crossing the Modi Khola river and ascending to the large Gurung village of Chhomrong. Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong. Explore this vibrant village — one of the largest on the Annapurna trek. Visit the local school, interact with Gurung community members, and browse the well-stocked shops. Rest at your lodge with unobstructed Annapurna views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a cultural evening — many lodges in Chhomrong host traditional Gurung cultural programs with folk music and dance (NPR 200–500 per person). Stargazing from the terrace is exceptional on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Tadapani lodge — muesli with milk, boiled eggs, black tea (NPR 350–550)
meals.lunch: Mid-trail tea house between Tadapani and Chhomrong — Tibetan bread with jam, soup (NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Chhomrong lodge — pizza (surprisingly good at altitude!), dal bhat, or pasta (NPR 600–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 11–13 km. Mixed terrain with significant descent and ascent. Trekking poles essential. Chhomrong is the last major resupply point before the Annapurna Sanctuary. Stock up on snacks, batteries, and any supplies needed.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Chhomrong. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Take a short acclimatization hike on the ridge above the village for panoramic views without significant elevation gain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chhomrong Khola waterfall (30-minute walk). Explore the traditional stone-paved village lanes. Visit the local tea house community center and learn about Gurung culture, traditions, and the history of the Annapurna region.
day_by_day.evening: Optional yoga or stretching session (some lodges offer guided sessions). Write postcards at the local post office. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and early rest to prepare for the ascent toward the Annapurna Base Camp.

meals.breakfast: Full western or Nepali breakfast at lodge — pancakes, honey, fresh ginger tea (NPR 450–750)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Chhomrong café — vegetable soup, garlic bread, fresh juice (NPR 400–700)
meals.dinner: Chhomrong lodge — thukpa (Tibetan noodle soup), momos (dumplings), masala chai (NPR 500–900)

day_by_day.notes: This rest day is essential for acclimatization before ascending to higher elevations (3,000m+). Drink 3–4 liters of water throughout the day. Avoid strenuous activity. Check weather forecasts for the upcoming days on the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Chhomrong early at 07:00. Trek to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) via Sinuwa and Bamboo — approximately 5–6 hours. The trail passes through dense bamboo and rhododendron forest, crossing several suspension bridges over the Modi Khola. Watch for Himalayan Tahr, langur monkeys, and colorful pheasants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Himalaya Hotel (a cluster of lodges, not a single hotel). Check in and rest. The dramatic narrowing of the valley walls creates an impressive gorge atmosphere. Short exploratory walk along the riverbank.
day_by_day.evening: The valley becomes very quiet and serene after dark. Enjoy the sound of the rushing Modi Khola river. Clear skies reveal a brilliant Milky Way. Early dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Chhomrong lodge — porridge, boiled eggs, black coffee (NPR 400–650)
meals.lunch: Bamboo tea house — dal bhat or fried rice (NPR 450–700). Note: prices increase with altitude
meals.dinner: Himalaya Hotel lodge — garlic soup (excellent for altitude), dal bhat, hot chocolate (NPR 600–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 10–12 km. Elevation gain: ~750m. The trail can be slippery after rain — gaiters recommended. Garlic soup is a traditional Himalayan remedy for altitude sickness — highly recommended at dinner. Temperatures drop significantly at night; ensure sleeping bag is rated to -5°C.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel to Deurali (3,230m) and on to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m) — approximately 5–6 hours total. The landscape transitions dramatically from forest to alpine meadow to glacial moraine. The iconic fishtail peak of Machhapuchhre dominates the skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at MBC by early afternoon. Rest and acclimatize — do not rush. Short walk on the moraine to observe the glacial landscape and approaching Annapurna Sanctuary amphitheater. The scale of the surrounding peaks is overwhelming.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset paint the Annapurna massif in shades of gold and pink from MBC. Temperatures will drop to -5°C or below — layer up. Early dinner and rest in preparation for the final push to ABC.

meals.breakfast: Himalaya Hotel lodge — toast, peanut butter, porridge, hot lemon tea (NPR 500–800)
meals.lunch: Deurali tea house — noodle soup, chocolate bar, electrolyte drink (NPR 500–800). Prices are high at altitude
meals.dinner: MBC lodge — garlic soup, dal bhat, hot ginger lemon honey drink (NPR 700–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 12–14 km. Elevation gain: ~780m. Signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea, dizziness) should be taken seriously — descend immediately if symptoms worsen. Drink 4+ liters of water. No alcohol at this altitude. Acclimatize slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Early start at 06:00. Trek from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130m) — approximately 2–3 hours. Arrive to the extraordinary 360-degree amphitheater of 8,000m peaks: Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, Khangsar Kang, and Machhapuchhre. This is the emotional and physical highlight of the entire journey. Spend time in quiet reflection at this sacred site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the ABC area — visit the memorial stones for mountaineers, walk the perimeter of the base camp plateau, photograph the glaciers and seracs. Rest at the lodge. Do not attempt any higher elevation without a guide and proper equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at ABC is extraordinary — the Annapurna massif turns deep orange and crimson. Celebrate reaching base camp with fellow trekkers over hot drinks. Early dinner and rest for the descent tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: MBC lodge — light breakfast before ascent: porridge, hot tea (NPR 500–700)
meals.lunch: ABC lodge — hot soup, crackers, chocolate (NPR 600–900). Eating at altitude can be difficult — eat small amounts frequently
meals.dinner: ABC lodge — dal bhat (the best meal for energy at altitude), hot chocolate, apple pie (NPR 800–1,400)

day_by_day.notes: ACHIEVEMENT UNLOCKED: Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Trek distance today: ~4–5 km. Oxygen levels are approximately 60% of sea level. Move slowly, breathe deeply. This is a bucket-list destination — take your time to absorb the experience. Night temperatures can drop to -10°C to -15°C. Ensure full cold-weather gear.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the magical ABC sunrise — watch the first light illuminate the Annapurna peaks in an unforgettable alpenglow display. After sunrise and breakfast, begin descent from ABC back to MBC and continue down to Bamboo (2,310m) — approximately 6–7 hours total descent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue steady descent through changing landscapes — from glacial moraine back through alpine meadow and into rhododendron and bamboo forest. The descent is much faster than the ascent. Arrive at Bamboo by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the warmer temperatures and thicker air at lower altitude. Rest your knees and legs. The sound of the forest and river is a welcome contrast to the stark high-altitude environment.

meals.breakfast: ABC lodge — eggs, toast, hot lemon tea before departure (NPR 600–900)
meals.lunch: MBC or Deurali tea house stop — dal bhat or noodles (NPR 500–800)
meals.dinner: Bamboo lodge — momos, thukpa, masala tea, rice pudding dessert (NPR 500–800)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 16–18 km (mostly descent). Descent is hard on the knees — use trekking poles and take your time on steep sections. Blisters are common on long descents — check and treat feet at day's end. Celebrate the successful ABC summit with fellow trekkers!

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Bamboo to Chhomrong (2,170m) — approximately 3–4 hours. The trail is now familiar and can be covered at a comfortable pace. Stop at Sinuwa for tea and views. Arrive in Chhomrong by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Chhomrong to Jhinu Danda (1,780m) — approximately 1.5–2 hours further descent. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola river. Spend the afternoon soaking in the therapeutic hot spring pools (NPR 200–300 entry fee) — a perfect reward after 10 days of trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight at a comfortable Jhinu Danda lodge. Enjoy a relaxed evening at lower altitude with warm temperatures. Watch the stars from the riverbank. Early rest for the final trekking day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Bamboo lodge — pancakes, honey, black tea (NPR 400–650)
meals.lunch: Chhomrong café — pizza, pasta, or dal bhat (NPR 600–1,000)
meals.dinner: Jhinu Danda lodge — grilled vegetables, rice, lentil soup, fresh fruit dessert (NPR 500–900)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 13–15 km. The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are a legendary trekking reward — do not miss them. Soak for 30–60 minutes to relieve muscle soreness. The spring water is naturally heated and rich in minerals. Bring flip-flops and a towel.

day_by_day.morning: Final trekking day: descend from Jhinu Danda to Nayapul (1,070m) — approximately 3–4 hours through terraced farmland and traditional Gurung villages. This is a beautiful, relaxed walk through rural Nepal. Arrive at Nayapul and take a local jeep or taxi back to Pokhara (1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Pokhara and return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Shower, change into clean clothes, and enjoy the luxury of a proper bed. Treat yourself to a traditional Nepali massage at one of Lakeside's many massage centers (60-minute full body massage: NPR 1,000–2,000). Stroll along Phewa Lake and reflect on the incredible journey.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at one of Pokhara's best restaurants. Browse the Lakeside market for final souvenirs — Thangka paintings, singing bowls, pashmina scarves, and handmade jewelry. Pack bags for departure or onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Jhinu Danda lodge — last trail breakfast: eggs, toast, porridge, ginger tea (NPR 400–650)
meals.lunch: Nayapul or roadside dhaba en route to Pokhara — dal bhat, fresh lassi (NPR 300–500)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Pokhara's Lakeside — Nepali thali platter, local Mustang wine or tongba (millet beer), dessert (NPR 1,200–2,500 per person). Recommended: Moondance, Caffe Concerto, or Lhasa Tibetan Restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Total trek completed: approximately 110–130 km over 10 trekking days, reaching 4,130m at Annapurna Base Camp. This is a world-class trekking achievement. Consider a domestic flight back to Kathmandu (25 min, ~USD 100–120) rather than the 7-hour bus for the return journey. Carry your ACAP and TIMS permits as souvenirs — they make wonderful mementos of the journey.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in a panoramic 180-degree view. The short but rewarding hike takes about 1.5 hours from Ghorepani village.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Welcome drink and late-night check-in with dedicated concierge assistance. Unwind in your Beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and herbal teas arranged in-room by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure passport, visa documents, and travel insurance are readily accessible. Nepal visa on arrival available at TIA. Private airport transfer should be pre-booked. Rest well — acclimatization begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start — enjoy a gourmet Himalayan breakfast on your private terrace overlooking the Annapurna range. Gentle orientation walk around the resort grounds with a naturalist guide to begin acclimatization. Breathe in the crisp mountain air and absorb the stunning panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided introductory nature walk through the surrounding rhododendron and oak forests near the resort. Learn about local flora, fauna, and Gurung culture from your expert guide. Visit a nearby traditional Gurung village for a cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's panoramic lounge with unobstructed Annapurna Himalaya views. Private welcome dinner with the resort's head chef presenting a curated Nepali tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet Himalayan breakfast spread on private terrace — fresh local honey, artisan breads, eggs cooked to order, seasonal fruits, and Nepali butter tea or French press coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's garden restaurant — grilled mountain trout, organic salads, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Private chef's tasting menu featuring Newari and Gurung cuisine — dal bhat with premium accompaniments, yak cheese appetizers, and traditional sel roti dessert paired with local Khukuri rum cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Day focused on rest and gentle acclimatization. Drink plenty of water, avoid alcohol in excess, and inform the concierge of any altitude sensitivity symptoms. Altitude at resort base is approximately 800–1,000m.

day_by_day.morning: After a nourishing breakfast, embark on a guided half-day hike through the Annapurna foothills — moderate terrain suitable for warming up trekking legs. Trail passes through terraced farmlands, suspension bridges over glacial rivers, and dense subtropical forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a post-hike luxury Himalayan spa treatment — traditional Ayurvedic massage using locally sourced herbs and oils. Relax by the resort's heated infinity pool with Himalayan backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset yoga session on the resort's mountain-facing deck led by a certified instructor. Followed by a candlelit dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Protein-rich trekking breakfast — scrambled eggs, smoked salmon, whole grain toast, fresh fruit platter, and Nepali masala chai
meals.lunch: Trail picnic lunch prepared by resort chefs — gourmet sandwiches, energy bars, fresh fruit, thermos of hot soup, and premium bottled water
meals.dinner: Candlelit à la carte dinner — Himalayan lamb chops, sautéed wild mushrooms, roasted root vegetables, and chocolate fondant with local cardamom ice cream, paired with imported wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper trekking boots and carry a daypack with water and sunscreen. The afternoon spa session should be booked in advance with the concierge. October weather typically clear and cool — ideal trekking conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for the iconic Poon Hill Sunrise Hike experience. Rise before dawn and begin the ascent to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m. Witness one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises with sweeping 180-degree views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Annapurna I.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Poon Hill through the charming trekking village of Ghorepani. Enjoy a warm lunch at a premium teahouse. Private vehicle return to resort. Afternoon at leisure — optional dip in the resort's heated pool or a relaxing nap.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at the resort to mark the completion of the iconic Poon Hill hike. Enjoy a bonfire evening with storytelling by a local cultural guide about Gurung traditions and Himalayan folklore.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn energy breakfast at resort before departure — oatmeal, boiled eggs, granola bars, and hot thermos of tea/coffee provided in packed form
meals.lunch: Premium teahouse lunch in Ghorepani — hearty dal bhat, vegetable curry, and fresh ginger lemon honey tea
meals.dinner: Celebratory bonfire dinner — Himalayan BBQ with marinated meats, roasted vegetables, artisan breads, and premium Nepali craft beer or imported spirits

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight experience of the trip. Depart resort no later than 03:30 AM to reach Poon Hill for sunrise. Dress in warm layers — temperatures at 3,210m before dawn can drop to near freezing in October. Headlamps, trekking poles, and warm gloves essential. Private guide mandatory.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Optional gentle stretching or yoga session to recover muscles from the Poon Hill hike. Explore the resort's curated library of Himalayan literature and photography books.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided cultural excursion to a nearby traditional Magar or Gurung village. Participate in a hands-on cooking class learning to prepare authentic Nepali dishes — dal bhat, gundruk soup, and momos — with a local family.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the dishes prepared during the cooking class for dinner. Private rooftop stargazing session with a telescope provided by the resort — the Annapurna region offers exceptional dark skies in October.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely brunch spread — Eggs Benedict, smoked meats, fresh-baked croissants, seasonal fruit, freshly squeezed juices, and specialty Nepali coffee
meals.lunch: Light resort café lunch — avocado toast, organic soups, and fresh herbal teas
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared during the afternoon cooking class served in a private dining setting — homemade momos, dal bhat, gundruk soup, and sel roti with honey

day_by_day.notes: Recovery day essential after Poon Hill. The cooking class must be arranged 24 hours in advance through the concierge. Stargazing session is weather dependent — confirm with resort staff.

day_by_day.morning: Guided bird-watching walk in the Annapurna Conservation Area — October is an excellent migration season. Spot Himalayan Monal (Nepal's national bird), danphe, eagles, and rare migratory species with an expert ornithologist guide. Binoculars and field guides provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive and short hike to the sacred Tal Barahi Temple or a nearby Buddhist monastery. Participate in a private meditation session led by a resident monk — a profoundly peaceful experience in the Himalayan setting.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset photography session at a scenic overlook with a professional photographer guide. Return to resort for a spa dinner — light, nourishing food designed for wellness and recovery.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before bird-watching — yogurt parfait, muesli, fresh fruit, and green tea
meals.lunch: Monastery-style vegetarian lunch — organic rice, lentil soup, seasonal vegetables, and herbal infusions
meals.dinner: Spa wellness dinner at the resort — steamed fish, quinoa, roasted vegetables, detox juices, and herbal teas

day_by_day.notes: Bird-watching walk begins at 06:00 AM when bird activity is highest. Wear muted, natural colors to avoid disturbing wildlife. The meditation session at the monastery requires modest dress — cover shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a full-day premium guided trek on a section of the Annapurna Circuit — one of the world's greatest trekking routes. Morning trail through lush subtropical forest, crossing traditional stone-paved paths used by local traders for centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through rhododendron forests and high-altitude meadows with continuous Annapurna Himalaya panoramas. Reach a scenic high point for a gourmet packed lunch with a view. Gradual descent back to the trailhead.
day_by_day.evening: Private vehicle return to resort. Luxury full-body recovery massage at the resort spa. Quiet dinner on the private terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: High-energy trekking breakfast — pancakes with local honey, scrambled eggs, fruit salad, and a thermos of hot coffee or tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet mountain picnic — chef-prepared sandwiches, cheese and charcuterie, dark chocolate, energy snacks, and hot soup in a thermos
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner — grilled Himalayan chicken, roasted potatoes, steamed greens, and a selection of Nepali desserts with imported wine

day_by_day.notes: Full-day trek — approximately 6–8 hours of hiking. Difficulty: moderate to moderately strenuous. Carry at least 2 liters of water, sunscreen, and a light rain jacket. October weather is generally excellent but afternoon clouds are possible.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter excursion over the Annapurna Sanctuary — a premium once-in-a-lifetime experience. Fly over the dramatic Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) glacier, the sacred Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain), and the entire Annapurna massif from above. Land at a high-altitude point for a champagne toast with Himalayan views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by helicopter to the resort. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the resort's luxury amenities, heated pool, or private Jacuzzi with mountain views. Optional in-room spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Special gala dinner at the resort's finest dining venue — a multi-course celebration dinner with wine pairing, live traditional Nepali music, and a cultural dance performance.

meals.breakfast: Pre-flight breakfast — light and energizing: fresh fruit, yogurt, toast, and herbal tea (avoid heavy meals before helicopter flight)
meals.lunch: Champagne and gourmet canapés served at the high-altitude helicopter landing point — a truly unique dining experience
meals.dinner: Multi-course gala dinner — amuse-bouche, Himalayan smoked salmon, yak tenderloin with truffle sauce, artisan cheese board, and dark chocolate mousse, paired with curated international wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter excursion is weather dependent and must be confirmed morning of. Costs are premium — arrange through the resort concierge well in advance. Weight limits apply for helicopter — pack light for this excursion. Champagne toast at altitude — drink responsibly given elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Guided nature photography walk through the Annapurna Conservation Area with a professional photographer. Learn techniques for capturing mountain landscapes, wildlife, and local culture. Visit scenic viewpoints and hidden trails not found on standard tourist maps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the enchanting Ghandruk village — one of the most beautiful Gurung settlements in the Annapurna region. Explore the Gurung Museum, traditional stone-paved alleys, and interact with local artisans. Purchase authentic handmade crafts and textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a Ghandruk viewpoint overlooking Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre. Return to resort for a relaxed dinner celebrating the midpoint of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Photographer's early breakfast — energy-boosting granola, eggs, toast, and strong coffee to prepare for the morning walk
meals.lunch: Traditional Gurung lunch in Ghandruk — locally prepared dal bhat with homemade pickles, raksi (local millet spirit) tasting, and fresh butter tea
meals.dinner: Relaxed resort dinner — wood-fired pizza with Himalayan toppings, fresh salads, and gelato dessert with local berry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Photography walk begins at 06:30 AM for best light. Bring or rent a quality camera — the resort can arrange equipment. Ghandruk is approximately 45 minutes from the resort by vehicle and short hike — comfortable footwear required.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium guided trek to Tadapani — a spectacular trail through dense rhododendron and magnolia forests offering continuous mountain views. The trail is less crowded than main circuit routes, offering a more exclusive wilderness experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tadapani (2,630m) for a warm teahouse lunch with extraordinary views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Explore the area before beginning the descent back through forest trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Relaxing soak in the resort's outdoor heated mineral bath. Light evening dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Full trekking breakfast — omelette, toast, porridge, fresh fruit, and a thermos of hot beverage for the trail
meals.lunch: Premium teahouse lunch at Tadapani — hearty vegetable noodle soup, dal bhat, and hot ginger tea
meals.dinner: Light and nourishing resort dinner — steamed momos, clear broth soup, fresh salad, and herbal infusions

day_by_day.notes: Tadapani trek is approximately 5–7 hours round trip. Moderate difficulty. The rhododendron forests are particularly beautiful in October. Carry rain gear as afternoon mist is possible at this elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed spa morning — begin with a Himalayan hot stone massage followed by a traditional Ayurvedic Shirodhara treatment (warm oil poured over the forehead). A deeply restorative experience after days of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) headquarters and visitor center to learn about conservation efforts, local biodiversity, and sustainable tourism in the region. Optional nature documentary screening at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class with the resort's head chef — learn to prepare a full Nepali feast from scratch. Enjoy the meal you've cooked as your dinner in a private dining room.

meals.breakfast: Wellness breakfast — smoothie bowls, chia pudding, fresh fruit, herbal teas, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Resort garden café — organic salads, grilled paneer, fresh-baked bread, and sparkling water with lemon and mint
meals.dinner: Self-prepared Nepali feast from the cooking class — sel roti, chicken curry, aloo tama (bamboo shoot and potato curry), and kheer (rice pudding) for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Spa treatments must be booked 24 hours in advance. The cooking class is an intimate 2–3 hour experience — inform the chef of any dietary restrictions. A wonderful way to take a piece of Nepal home with you.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike to a local viewpoint near the resort for a final intimate Himalayan sunrise experience. Return for a leisurely breakfast. Morning at leisure — last opportunity for a swim in the resort pool or a walk through the resort gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic guided nature walk through the Modi Khola river valley — following the rushing glacial river through dramatic gorges, hanging bridges, and lush riparian forest. A beautiful and relatively gentle walk perfect for the penultimate active day.
day_by_day.evening: Private farewell cocktail reception hosted by the resort manager on the panoramic rooftop terrace. Followed by a premium farewell dinner with the finest dishes from across the 14-day journey.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely farewell breakfast — full gourmet spread with all favorite items from the trip, freshly baked pastries, and specialty Himalayan coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside picnic lunch in the Modi Khola valley — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, artisan cheeses, and cold brew coffee
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — five-course meal featuring the best of Nepali and international cuisine, premium wine pairing, and a special dessert platter with a personalized Himalayan chocolate creation

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise viewpoint hike departs at 05:30 AM — optional but highly recommended for a final magical Himalayan moment. Farewell dinner is a special occasion — smart casual dress encouraged. Begin packing non-essential items tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort. Last Himalayan breakfast on the private terrace. Checkout formalities handled by the dedicated concierge team. Farewell to the resort staff.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury vehicle transfer from Annapurna region to Pokhara or Kathmandu (depending on departure logistics). En route, stop at scenic viewpoints for final photographs of the Annapurna range. Optional visit to the Pokhara lakeside or Kathmandu's Thamel for last-minute premium souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium Kathmandu or Pokhara hotel if overnight stay required before departure flight. Relaxed dinner at one of the city's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a personal selection of all favorite dishes from the trip
meals.lunch: En route lunch at a premium restaurant in Pokhara — lakeside dining with views of Phewa Lake and the Annapurna range
meals.dinner: Premium dinner in Kathmandu or Pokhara — Nepali fine dining at a top-rated restaurant such as Krishnarpan (Kathmandu) or Caffe Concerto (Pokhara)

day_by_day.notes: Transfer from Annapurna region to Kathmandu is approximately 6–7 hours by road or 25 minutes by domestic flight from Pokhara. Confirm transfer arrangements with the concierge 48 hours in advance. Keep essential documents, valuables, and a change of clothes in your carry-on.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal. If time permits before departure, visit Pashupatinath Temple or Boudhanath Stupa in Kathmandu for a spiritual send-off — both UNESCO World Heritage Sites within easy reach of the airport. Alternatively, enjoy a final spa treatment at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Departure formalities — allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure. Duty-free shopping for last-minute Nepali handicrafts, pashmina, and teas.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Nepal with extraordinary memories of the Annapurna Himalayas, world-class trekking, and the warmth of Nepali hospitality. Safe travels home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light and travel-friendly: yogurt, fruit, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining or a final meal at a quality Kathmandu restaurant near the airport
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Reconfirm return flight details 24 hours prior. Nepali Rupees can be exchanged back to foreign currency at the airport (keep exchange receipts). Declare any items of value purchased during the trip as required by customs. Weight limits for luggage may have changed if you've purchased souvenirs — check airline policy.
